interactions.name: Partner color identity
interactions.finding: Rograkh is red and Silas Renn is blue-black; together the commanders establish U/B/R color identity for deck construction.

interactions.name: Rograkh zero-mana resource engine
interactions.finding: Rograkh can be cast for zero mana before commander tax and provides a legendary/red creature for Mox Amber, Springleaf Drum, Paradise Mantle, Culling the Weak, Infernal Plunge, Diabolic Intent, commander-presence free spells, Jeska's Will, and Flare of Duplication. Later commander-tax casts require the applicable additional cost.

interactions.name: Silas Renn artifact recursion
interactions.finding: After Silas deals combat damage to a player, his trigger targets an artifact card in its controller's graveyard and grants permission to cast that card that turn; normal timing restrictions still apply unless another effect changes them.

interactions.name: Thassa's Oracle + Demonic Consultation / Tainted Pact
interactions.finding: The candidate preserves the compact Oracle library-exhaustion wins. Tainted Pact's construction requirement is supported by 100 distinct card names.

interactions.name: Underworld Breach + Lion's Eye Diamond + Brain Freeze
interactions.finding: With sufficient graveyard material and spell count, LED supplies mana while Brain Freeze's storm copies replenish the graveyard, allowing repeated escapes that mill libraries and/or build a winning storm sequence.

interactions.name: Underworld Breach + Grinding Station + zero-mana artifact
interactions.finding: Grinding Station untaps when an artifact enters. With Breach and a reusable zero-mana artifact such as Mox Amber, the artifact can be used, sacrificed to Station, and escaped using cards milled by Station, producing repeated mill/storm; Rograkh enables Mox Amber to make red mana.

interactions.name: Final Fortune / Warrior's Oath
interactions.finding: Each creates an extra turn and a delayed triggered ability that causes its controller to lose at the beginning of that extra turn's end step. The line must win or otherwise answer/end around that trigger rather than treating the extra turn as consequence-free.

interactions.name: Samut, Tyrant of Naktamun split second
interactions.finding: Samut gives instant and sorcery spells its controller controls split second. While such a spell is on the stack, players cannot cast spells or activate nonmana abilities, but triggered abilities still trigger and resolve normally.

interactions.name: Vexing Bauble symmetry
interactions.finding: Bauble triggers on any spell cast without mana spent to cast it, including the controller's own zero-mana or free/alternate-cost spells. Spending commander tax on a later Rograkh cast counts as mana spent. Bauble can be sacrificed for its draw ability before a planned free-spell sequence.

interactions.name: Vexing Bauble + Hexing Squelcher
interactions.finding: Bauble may still trigger on a no-mana-spent spell controlled by the RogSi player, but Hexing Squelcher makes that player's spells unable to be countered, so Bauble cannot successfully counter them while Squelcher is active.

interactions.name: Vexing Bauble + Samut
interactions.finding: Split second does not suppress triggered abilities. Vexing Bauble therefore still triggers on a Samut-granted split-second instant or sorcery if no mana was spent to cast it.

interactions.name: Demonic Counsel
interactions.finding: Without delirium, Demonic Counsel searches only for a Demon card; this candidate contains no Demon card, so a pre-delirium search cannot find a card. With four or more card types in the graveyard, delirium replaces that restriction and it becomes an unrestricted tutor.

interactions.name: Mnemonic Betrayal
interactions.finding: Mnemonic Betrayal exiles cards from opponents' graveyards and permits casting those cards that turn with mana flexibility. It does not grant permission to play lands; uncast exiled cards return at the next end step, and Betrayal exiles itself.

interactions.name: Undercity Sewers
interactions.finding: Undercity Sewers is a front-face land with Island and Swamp types, enters tapped, and surveils 1; it is therefore fetchable by the candidate's appropriate fetchlands and counts as one of the 24 land slots.
